_readme: The shared vocabulary of Posnic: one row per term, every language side by side.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Tamil was translated key by key over several years, and it
shows. 'Apply' and 'Search' ended up sharing a word. 'Item position' was labelled
with the words for 'branch access'. Every Edit button read as 'Edited', in the past
tense. None of those is a translation mistake by anybody. It is what happens when
the same English word is translated seven times by people who cannot see each
other's work. A term settled here is settled once, for every screen at once.
HOW IT IS USED. tests/tools/seed-from-glossary.js fills languages/<code>.json for
any key whose English matches a term here exactly. It NEVER overwrites a
translation somebody has already written: your work always wins over this file.
HOW TO CHANGE IT. Edit the row, run the seeder, commit both. If a term here is
wrong for your language, that matters more than any single key - it is wrong on
every screen at once, and fixing the row fixes all of them together.
A BLANK IS NOT A GAP TO FILL WITH A GUESS. Blanks are deliberate. They are terms
nobody has confidently settled, and the app shows English for them, which is
correct and readable. A word that is wrong is worse than a word that is English.
This file is not shipped to the app. It is the source the packs are built from.
brandsReadme: Names, not words. A brand, a product and a barcode symbology are spelled the
same in every language - a payment tab that reads "Provider Way2sms" no longer
names the provider the shopkeeper is looking for. Six translators changed these
anyway, because a validator that rejects a value identical to its English left
them no other way to pass. The rule is enforced by tests/i18n.test.js now, so
nobody has to fight it again.
Descriptive names are NOT here: Soft Dark, Warm Night and Diamond are words, and
a theme picker in Thai should read in Thai.

notes.Register: The cash drawer a cashier opens at the start of a shift. NOT the verb 'to register' and not a signup. If your language would read it as 'sign up', use your words for 'cash drawer' or 'till' instead.
notes.Receiving: Goods arriving from a supplier and being taken into stock. A noun here, never the verb.
notes.Return: Goods coming back from a customer. Several languages use the same word as 'Back', the navigation control. That is usually fine, but check it still reads as a refund on the sale screen.
notes.Branch: One shop or outlet of a business that has several. The bank-branch word usually works.
notes.Item: What the shop sells. Some shops sell services with no stock, so avoid a word that means physical goods exclusively.
notes.Credit: On the customer screens this is money the customer owes the shop. On the payment screens it can mean a card. Check which screen a key belongs to before settling it.
notes.Store: The shop itself. Not the verb 'to store'.
notes.State: The region in a postal address, not a status. Use the word your country's address forms use.
notes.Table: A restaurant table people sit at, not a table of data.
notes.Tax: The generic word. GST, CGST, SGST and IGST are Indian statutory names and stay in Latin script exactly as they are - a shopkeeper matches them against a government form.
notes.Qty: Deliberately abbreviated: it is a narrow column heading. If your language has no natural short form, the full word is better than an invented abbreviation.
notes.Sale: One transaction at the counter. 'Sales' is the list of them, and some languages need a different word for each.
